title: The changing frame
description: A moving aperture reframes a woodblock print while the artwork remains completely still.
useCase: Compare publishing formats while preserving subject scale and showing which parts of an artwork will be cropped.

assets.description: Shower Below the Summit (Sanka hakuu), from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, Katsushika Hokusai

reducedMotion: Format and crop position change immediately; the complete artwork remains visible as a faint context layer.
limitations: Three authored crop positions, not automatic focal-point detection or a draggable/exporting image editor. Clip-path and bounded frame geometry animate; this is not a compositor-only effect. Sample artwork is a separately declared CC0 asset.
look: Off-white page with a Japanese woodblock print of a red mountain, vivid inside corner-marked crop bounds and faded beyond them, above a segmented control.
motion: Choosing 4:5, 1:1 or 16:9 animates a clip-path aperture and its corner marks to the new crop over 620 ms with an ease-out, while the artwork stays still.
adapt: The `fc-aperture` clip-path `inset(${y}px ${420 - x - format.width}px ${y}px ${x}px)` and the four fixed-size marks inside `fc-crop-edge` share `620ms cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.18,1)`. Each mark translates to its crop corner without resizing its box; the clip-path still has its own rendering cost. Crops come from `formats` in a fixed 420×278 stage. Replace `src` and `alt`, then match image dimensions and crop offsets.
